By \(\texttt{lem:ridge-loss-expansion}\), jointly for the two roles,
\[
 \sqrt n\{(\widehat L_1-\widehat L_2)-(L_1-L_2)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{t=1}^n\{(\ell_{1,t}-L_1)-(\ell_{2,t}-L_2)\}+o_{P_n}(1).
\]
The stipulated centered Gaussian limit, \(\texttt{ass:local-loss-gap}\), and \(D=Q_1-Q_2\) yield
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat L_1-\widehat L_2)\Rightarrow d+D.
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:selector-variance-margin}\), \(\operatorname{Var}(D)\geq\nu>0\).  Hence \(d+D\) has no atom at zero, even if the complete stacked covariance is singular, and the tie rule implies
\[
 \widehat J\Rightarrow J(d),\qquad
 J(d)=1\text{ on }\{d+D\leq0\},\quad J(d)=2\text{ otherwise}.
\]
More explicitly, the probability of the discontinuity strip is bounded by \(2\epsilon/\sqrt{2\pi\nu}\), so continuous upper and lower interpolations followed by \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) justify this indicator mapping.

For each role, \(\texttt{lem:fixed-role-linearization}\) gives
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_s-\tau)
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{t=1}^n\psi_{s,t}
 +\sqrt{n/m}\,m^{-1/2}\sum_{t=n+1}^{n+m}v_{s,t}+o_{P_n}(1).
\]
The joint Gaussian premise, independence of the post limit from the pre limit, and \(n/m\to r\) from \(\texttt{ass:sample-ratio}\) therefore imply
\[
 \left(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_1-\tau),\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_2-\tau),
 \sqrt n(\widehat L_1-\widehat L_2)\right)
 \Rightarrow(A_1+\sqrt rR_1,A_2+\sqrt rR_2,d+D).
\]
The switching map is discontinuous only when \(d+D=0\), a null event.  Thus
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sel}}-\tau)
 \Rightarrow A_{J(d)}+\sqrt rR_{J(d)}.
\]

By \(\texttt{lem:conventional-hac-consistency}\),
\[
 \max_{s\in\mathcal S}|\widehat V_s^{\mathrm{conv}}-V_s|\to_{P_n}0,
 \qquad
 \Pr_{P_n}\{\min_s\widehat V_s^{\mathrm{conv}}\geq\nu/2\}\to1.
\]
Selection cannot enlarge the maximum error.  On this event the inverse square-root map is Lipschitz with a constant depending only on \(\nu\); tightness of the selected numerator makes replacement of the true inverse standard deviation by the estimated one an \(o_{P_n}(1)\) perturbation, and continuous upper and lower approximations therefore give
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sel}}-\tau}
 {\widehat{\operatorname{se}}^{\mathrm{conv}}_{\widehat J}}
 \Rightarrow
 \frac{A_1+\sqrt rR_1}{\sqrt{V_1}}\mathbf1\{d+D\leq0\}
 +\frac{A_2+\sqrt rR_2}{\sqrt{V_2}}\mathbf1\{d+D>0\}.
\]
Since \(X=D/\sigma_D\) and \(k=-d/\sigma_D\), this is exactly
\[
 T_1\mathbf1\{X\leq k\}+T_2\mathbf1\{X>k\}.
\]
If a role is fixed, the indicators disappear and \(T_s\sim N(0,1)\), because \(V_s=\operatorname{Var}(A_s+\sqrt rR_s)>0\).  On a separate sequence with \(|\sqrt n(L_1-L_2)|\to\infty\), the centered loss fluctuation is tight and the population sign selects one role with probability tending to one, giving the same reduction.  Proposition \(\texttt{prop:shi-anchor-transfer}\) places the explicit stationary square family in the intersection with Shi et al.'s fixed-role class.  This proves only the stated common-subclass comparison, not inclusion of either full class in the other and not a claim about the rectangular application rule.

Each \(T_s\) is marginally standard normal and \(X\) is standard normal.  The boundary of the selected coverage event is contained in \(\{T_1=\pm z\}\cup\{T_2=\pm z\}\cup\{X=k\}\), which has probability zero.  Hence \(\texttt{thm:selected-gaussian-limit}\) transfers finite-sample coverage to the selected Gaussian probability.  For \(|\rho_s|<1\), completing the square in the bivariate Gaussian density gives
\[
 T_s\mid X=x\sim N(\rho_sx,1-\rho_s^2),
\]
and therefore \(\Pr(|T_s|\leq z\mid X=x)=g_{\rho_s}(x;z)\).  Conditioning on \(X\) proves
\[
 \Pr(|T_1|\leq z,X\leq k)+\Pr(|T_2|\leq z,X>k)=C_z(k).
\]
The endpoint cases \(|\rho_s|=1\) follow from the degenerate conditional identity \(T_s=\rho_sX\), equivalently by continuity.

Symmetry of \([-z,z]\) gives
\[
 g_\rho(-x;z)=g_\rho(x;z),
 \qquad
 \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\phi(x)g_\rho(x;z)\,dx=2\Phi(z)-1.
\]
Thus each half-line through zero contributes half of the unselected coverage, and \(C_z(0)=2\Phi(z)-1\) for arbitrary \(\rho_1,\rho_2\).

For \(a,z>0\) and \(q\in[0,1]\), let \(R_z(a,q)=\Pr_q(|X|\leq a,|T|\leq z)\), where the bivariate standard normal pair has correlation \(q\).  Symmetric rectangles make this quantity depend on a correlation only through its absolute value.  For \(0<q<1\), direct differentiation of the density \(f_q\) gives \(\partial_qf_q=\partial_x\partial_tf_q\).  Integration over \([-a,a]\times[-z,z]\) yields
\[
 \frac{\partial R_z(a,q)}{\partial q}
 =2\{f_q(a,z)-f_q(a,-z)\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{f_q(a,z)}{f_q(a,-z)}
 =\exp\left(\frac{2qaz}{1-q^2}\right)>1.
\]
Hence \(R_z(a,q)\) is strictly increasing in \(q\in[0,1]\), with endpoints obtained by continuity.  Evenness now gives, for \(k\ne0\),
\[
 C_z(k)-\{2\Phi(z)-1\}
 =\frac{\operatorname{sign}(k)}2
 \{R_z(|k|,|\rho_1|)-R_z(|k|,|\rho_2|)\}.
\]
The strict sign assertion follows.  If \(\rho_1^2=\rho_2^2\), then \(g_{\rho_1}=g_{\rho_2}\) and coverage is nominal for every \(k\).  Conversely, nominal coverage for every \(k\), together with the strict display at any \(k\ne0\), forces \(\rho_1^2=\rho_2^2\).  This proves the frontier, including all degenerate-correlation endpoints.

Put \(e_{0t}^{\star}=e_{0t}+\xi_t\) and \(\bar b=b+\zeta\).  By \(\texttt{def:primitive-gaussian-family}\), \(F_t,e_{0t}^{\star},e_{1t},e_{2t}\) are mutually independent, apart from \(\mathbb E_nF_t=\mu\), and
\[
 Y_t(0)=F_t+e_{0t}^{\star},\qquad \Delta_t=\tau.
\]
Thus the separately defined causal target satisfies \(\mathbb E_n\Delta_t=\tau\).  The rows are stationary and independent over time, have moments of every order, and have \(\beta_n(j)=0\) for \(j\geq1\).

Write \(B=\mathbb E_nF_t^2=\mu^2+f\).  Independence and centering give, for either exchange of donor and proxy,
\[
 M_s=c_1c_{2,n}B,\qquad
 \mathbb E_n(W_{2t}Y_t(0))=c_{2,n}B,\qquad
 \mathbb E_n(W_{1t}Y_t(0))=c_1B.
\]
Since \(B,c_1,c_{2,n}>0\) eventually,
\[
 \alpha_1=c_1^{-1},\qquad \alpha_2=c_{2,n}^{-1},
\]
and the two bridge residuals are \(e_{0t}^{\star}-e_{1t}\) and \(e_{0t}^{\star}-e_{2t}\).  They are centered, so \(\texttt{ass:bridge-centering}\) holds.  In the post period,
\[
 \mathbb E_n\{Y_t(0)+\Delta_t-W_{jt}\alpha_j\}=\tau,
\]
which proves that the observed bridge residual identifies the causal target rather than defining it.  At the tied limit the scalar bridge singular value is \(B/\sqrt{t_1t_2}\).

For a generic donor \(W_j=c_j(F+e_j)\), with \(q_1=x,q_2=y\) and \(c_j^2=t_j^{-1}\), the ridge normal equation gives
\[
 a_j=\frac{c_jB}{1+c_j^2(B+q_j)},
 \qquad
 W_ja_j=\frac{B}{t_j+B+q_j}(F+e_j).
\]
Completing the square gives
\[
 L_j=\mathbb E_n\{Y_t(0)^2\}-\frac{B^2}{t_j+B+q_j}.
\]
The tied equality \(t_2=t_1+x-y\) makes both denominators equal \(R\).  With \(\delta_n=(R^2/B^2)d/\sqrt n\) and \(t_{2,n}=t_2-\delta_n\), positivity holds eventually and
\[
 L_1-L_2=\frac{B^2}{R-\delta_n}-\frac{B^2}{R}
 =\frac d{\sqrt n}\frac{R}{R-\delta_n}
 =\frac d{\sqrt n}+O(n^{-1}).
\]
This proves the local-loss calibration.  Finitely many initial rows may be set equal to the tied law without changing any limit or strict eventual margin.

At the tied limit set \(U_0=(1-\eta)F+e_0^{\star}\).  The centered one-period loss contrast is
\[
 \delta\ell_t=-2\eta U_0(e_1-e_2)+\eta^2(e_1^2-e_2^2+y-x).
\]
The definitions of \(H_s,u_{s,t},\psi_{s,t}\), together with \(K=\mu/B\), give
\[
 \psi_{1,t}=-K(F_t+e_{2t})(e_{0t}^{\star}-e_{1t}),
 \qquad
 \psi_{2,t}=-K(F_t+e_{1t})(e_{0t}^{\star}-e_{2t}),
\]
and constant treatment gives \(v_{1,t}=e_{0t}^{\star}-e_{1t}\), \(v_{2,t}=e_{0t}^{\star}-e_{2t}\).  All stacked scores are degree-two Gaussian polynomials.  For any coefficient vector \(a\), Taylor expansion of the one-period characteristic function gives
\[
 \mathbb E_n\exp\{\mathrm ia^{\prime}G_t/\sqrt n\}
 =1-\frac{a^{\prime}\Sigma_na}{2n}+O(n^{-3/2}).
\]
Independence over time, convergence of \(\Sigma_n\), and exponentiation prove convergence of every displayed multivariate characteristic function to that of the asserted, possibly singular, joint Gaussian law.  Disjoint pre and post samples are independent.

The two summands of \(\delta\ell_t\) are uncorrelated because every cross term contains an odd centered Gaussian moment.  Since
\[
 \mathbb E_nU_0^2=(1-\eta)^2B+\bar b,\quad
 \mathbb E_n(e_1-e_2)^2=x+y,\quad
 \operatorname{Var}(e_1^2-e_2^2)=2(x^2+y^2),
\]
we obtain
\[
 \sigma_D^2=4\eta^2\{(1-\eta)^2B+\bar b\}(x+y)
 +2\eta^4(x^2+y^2).
\]
Conditioning on \((F,e_0^{\star})\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E[(e_1-e_2)(F+e_2)(e_0^{\star}-e_1)\mid F,e_0^{\star}]
 =-xF-ye_0^{\star}.
\]
The quadratic part of \(\delta\ell_t\) again has zero covariance with \(\psi_{1,t}\), so
\[
 c_{D1}=-2\eta K\{(1-\eta)Bx+\bar b y\}.
\]
Exchanging roles yields
\[
 c_{D2}=2\eta K\{(1-\eta)By+\bar b x\}.
\]
The two factors in each pre-score product are independent and the residual factor is centered.  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(A_1)=K^2(B+y)(\bar b+x),
 \quad \operatorname{Var}(A_2)=K^2(B+x)(\bar b+y),
\]
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(R_1)=\bar b+x,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(R_2)=\bar b+y,
\]
and hence the displayed formulas for \(V_1,V_2\) in the target follow.  Independence of \(R_s\) from \(D\) gives \(\rho_s=c_{Ds}/\sqrt{\sigma_D^2V_s}\).

At \(\theta_0\), direct substitution gives
\[
 \bar b=1,\quad B=2,\quad R=4,\quad \eta=K=\tfrac12,
 \quad \sigma_D^2=\tfrac{13}4,\quad c_{D1}=-1,\quad c_{D2}=1,
 \quad V_1=V_2=\tfrac32+2r.
\]
Thus \(\rho_1=-\rho_2\).  If \(Z_s=A_s+\sqrt rR_s\), Gaussian conditioning gives \(\mathbb E(Z_s\mid X)=c_{Ds}X/\sigma_D\).  Since
\[
 \mathbb E\{X\mathbf1(X\leq k)\}=-\phi(k),\qquad
 \mathbb E\{X\mathbf1(X>k)\}=\phi(k),
\]
the selected limiting ATT coordinate has mean
\[
 \frac{c_{D2}-c_{D1}}{\sigma_D}\phi(k)=\frac2{\sigma_D}\phi(k)>0
\]
for every finite \(k\), although \(\texttt{thm:wald-symmetry-frontier}\) gives exact symmetric coverage.  Its bridge singular value is \(2\), and all asserted rank, variance, and moment margins are therefore strict under the numerical restrictions in the proposition.

At \(\theta_a\), \(\bar b=1/10\), \(B=2\), \(R=4\), and \(\eta=K=1/2\).  Exact substitution gives
\[
 \sigma_D^2=\frac{161}{100},\quad c_{D1}=-\frac{19}{100},
 \quad c_{D2}=\frac{91}{100},\quad
 V_1=\frac{63}{200},\quad V_2=\frac{247}{200},
\]
and
\[
 \rho_1=-\frac{19\sqrt2}{\sqrt{10143}}=-0.2667997301850519\ldots,
 \qquad
 \rho_2=\frac{91\sqrt2}{\sqrt{39767}}=0.6453494964281337\ldots.
\]
Here \(B/\sqrt{t_1t_2}=10/3\), so the stated \(\kappa,\nu\), and moment restrictions make the point legal.  With \(d/\sigma_D=-1\), one has \(k=1\).  Direct interval evaluation of the defining integrals, using directed rounding on \([-12,1]\) and \([1,12]\), gives respectively
\[
 [0.7601411914468526,0.7601411914468528],
 \qquad
 [0.1256345996182179,0.1256345996182181].
\]
The omitted Gaussian mass is below \(4\times10^{-33}\), so
\[
 C_{\Phi^{-1}(0.95)}(1)
 \in[0.8857757910650705,0.8857757910650709].
\]
Independently of decimal evaluation, \(\rho_1^2<\rho_2^2\) and \(k>0\), so the strict sign theorem proves coverage below \(0.9\).  The path is \(t_{2,n}=1/5-4d/\sqrt n\), hence is eventually positive.  All formulas and strict inequalities are continuous on their positive-denominator domain, proving strict undercoverage on a relatively open legal neighborhood.  Relabeling the roles reverses the squared-correlation ordering, and reversing \(d\) reverses \(k\), giving the asserted overcoverage realization.

Finally, conditional on \(F_t\), the treated idiosyncratic error and both measurement errors are mutually independent; the loading identity is \(c_j\alpha_j=1\); the rank matrix is \(c_1c_{2,n}B>0\); and treatment is constant.  Proposition \(\texttt{prop:shi-anchor-transfer}\) verifies Shi et al.'s listed conditions on compact neighborhoods with these strict margins.  This completes every realization claim.

If role \(s\) is fixed before observing the panel, \(\texttt{lem:fixed-role-linearization}\), the Gaussian premise used in \(\texttt{thm:selected-gaussian-limit}\), and conventional HAC consistency give
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_s-\tau)\Rightarrow A_s+\sqrt rR_s,
 \qquad
 \frac{\widehat\tau_s-\tau}{\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_s^{\mathrm{conv}}}
 \Rightarrow T_s\sim N(0,1).
\]
Thus symmetric Wald coverage tends to \(2\Phi(z)-1\).  If \(\sqrt n(L_1-L_2)\to+\infty\), the ridge expansion writes the empirical contrast as the diverging term plus \(O_{P_n}(1)\), so \(\Pr(\widehat J=2)\to1\); a negative divergence selects role one.  Substitution yields the same fixed-role limit.

For the split construction, fixing a role removes only the random label.  Since
\[
 N_{B,n}=n-\lfloor\varrho n\rfloor-\lceil(\log n)^2\rceil
 =(1-\varrho)n+o(n),
\]
the fixed-role late/post linearization has root-\(n\) variance
\[
 V_s^{\mathrm{gap}}=\frac{\Omega_{\psi,s}}{1-\varrho}+r\Omega_{v,s}
 =V_s+\frac{\varrho}{1-\varrho}\Omega_{\psi,s}\geq V_s.
\]
This is ordinary fixed-role late-block proximal inference with its split-sample variance, not the full-pre-period efficiency bound.

For a fixed row write \(\varepsilon_{0t}=e_{0t}+\xi_t\), \(\varepsilon_{1t}=c_1e_{1t}\), and \(\varepsilon_{2t}=c_{2,n}e_{2t}\).  Then
\[
 Y_t(0)=F_t+\varepsilon_{0t},\qquad
 W_{1t}=c_1F_t+\varepsilon_{1t},\qquad
 W_{2t}=c_{2,n}F_t+\varepsilon_{2t}.
\]
The three errors are mutually independent conditional on \(F_t\), so either exchange of donor and supplemental proxy satisfies conditional proxy independence and exclusion.  Consistency and no anticipation hold by the definition of \(Y_t\), and \(\Delta_t=\tau\) proves \(\mathbb E_n\Delta_t=\tau\).

For donor \(j\) and opposite proxy \(k\), \(\alpha_j=1/c_j\), \(c_j\alpha_j=1\), and
\[
 M_s=\mathbb E_n(W_{kt}W_{jt})=c_kc_jB>0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_n(W_{kt}Y_t(0))=c_kB=M_s\alpha_j.
\]
The bridge is therefore unique and full rank, and its centered residual is \(\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{jt}\).  Hence
\[
 \mathbb E_n\{Y_t(0)+\Delta_t-W_{jt}\alpha_j\}=\tau,
\]
which derives identification from the structural bridge.

The observations are independent and identically distributed over time, hence stationary, ergodic, and absolutely regular with zero positive-lag coefficients.  Gaussian rows have all moments and a Lebesgue density.  On a compact parameter neighborhood bounded away from zero factor, error, scaling, rank, and fixed-role variance coordinates, the moments have a common integrable envelope.  The moment maps are polynomial in observations and continuously differentiable in the bridge and ATT parameters.  The bridge derivative is \(-M_s\ne0\) and the ATT derivative is \(-1\), so the fixed-role Jacobian is triangular and nonsingular; laws of large numbers give sample-Jacobian convergence.  The pre bridge score and post residual have strictly positive variances because \(\mathbb E_nW_{kt}^2>0\) and \(b+\zeta+\operatorname{Var}(e_{jt})>0\).  These facts, compactness, and comparable horizons verify the stated fixed-role regularity and supplementary conditions.

In the diagonal family used below, the exceptional treated error is
\[
 \varepsilon_{0t}^{(q)}=I_{q,t}-p_q+a_qZ_{0t},\qquad p_q=q^{-2},\quad a_q=q^{-4}.
\]
It is centered, has a strictly positive Lebesgue density, has uniformly bounded moments of every fixed order, and is independent of the factor and both Gaussian measurement errors.  Those errors have variance \(a_q^2>0\).  Thus each row retains domination, conditional proxy independence, positive fixed-role covariance, nonsingular Jacobian, full bridge rank, constant treatment, and comparable horizons.  This proves the rowwise published-class membership of the diagonal witness.  The argument is an intersection certificate only: it proves neither full-class inclusion direction.

Set
\[
 B_0=\frac{6373}{30000},\qquad x_0=\frac18,
 \qquad \bar b_0=\frac78,qquad t_0=\frac{5123}{10000},
 \qquad c_0=t_0^{-1/2}.
\]
Then
\[
 t_0+B_0+x_0=4B_0,qquad \eta_0=\frac14,qquad
 c_0^2B_0=\frac{B_0}{t_0}=\frac{6373}{15369}>\kappa.
\]
Set \(m_j=j\), so \(j/m_j=1\).

For each sufficiently large integer \(q\), define a whole array \(P_\bullet^{(q)}\).  Every row is independent and identically distributed over the two-sided time index.  In each row \(j\ne q\), generate mutually independent
\[
 F_t\sim N(0,B_0),\quad e_{1t},e_{2t}\sim N(0,x_0),
 \quad \varepsilon_{0t}\sim N(0,\bar b_0),
\]
and set
\[
 Y_t(0)=F_t+\varepsilon_{0t},\quad \Delta_t=\tau,
 \quad W_{1t}=c_0(F_t+e_{1t}),\quad W_{2t}=c_0(F_t+e_{2t}).
\]
In row \(j=q\), retain \(F_t\sim N(0,B_0)\), put \(p_q=q^{-2}\), \(a_q=q^{-4}\), generate mutually independent
\[
 I_{q,t}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_q),qquad
 Z_{0t},Z_{1t},Z_{2t}\sim N(0,1),
\]
and use the same observation equations with
\[
 \varepsilon_{0t}=I_{q,t}-p_q+a_qZ_{0t},qquad
 e_{1t}=a_qZ_{1t},qquad e_{2t}=a_qZ_{2t}.
\]
The rare centered component is thus in the untreated-outcome error and treatment remains constant.  Conditional on \(F_t\), all three idiosyncratic errors are independent, and \(\mathbb E_{P_j^{(q)}}\Delta_t=\tau\).

We verify membership in \(\mathcal M(0)\).  Independence over time proves stationarity and \(\beta_j(h)=0\) for \(h\geq1\).  Gaussian scales are bounded, \(0\leq I_{q,t}\leq1\), and \(a_q,p_q\leq1\), so one finite \(C_{\mathrm{mom}}\) bounds all required moments over \(j,q\).  For either role and every row,
\[
 M_s=c_0^2B_0=\frac{6373}{15369}>\kappa,qquad
 \mathbb E(Z_{s,t}Y_t(0))=c_0B_0=M_s/c_0.
\]
Therefore \(\alpha_s=c_0^{-1}\), and the bridge residual is \(\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{s,t}\), where \(e_{s,t}\) is the selected donor's measurement error.  It is centered, and
\[
 \mathbb E\{Y_t(0)+\Delta_t-W_{D_s,t}\alpha_s\}=\tau.
\]
The two controls have identical joint second moments with the treated outcome in every row, so their population ridge coefficients and losses coincide: \(L_{1,j}=L_{2,j}\).  Thus the bounded selector-gap condition holds with envelope zero.

Since \(\mathbb EW_{D_s,t}=0\), \(H_s=0\), \(\psi_{s,t}=0\), and \(A_s=0\).  All rows after \(q\) equal the ordinary Gaussian row, so their long-run covariance matrices are constant and converge to a finite positive-semidefinite matrix.  The stacked limit is singular because both pre-ATT coordinates vanish.  A possibly singular Gaussian limit nevertheless exists: for the ordinary-row centered score vector \(G_t\) and every fixed \(u\),
\[
 \mathbb E\exp(\mathrm iu^{\prime}G_t/\sqrt j)
 =1-\frac{u^{\prime}\Sigma_Gu}{2j}+O(j^{-3/2}),
\]
and independence followed by exponentiation proves convergence of every multivariate characteristic function to the possibly singular Gaussian characteristic function, without covariance inversion.

For an ordinary row the ridge fitted value is \(\eta_0(F_t+e_{jt})\).  With \(U_t=(1-\eta_0)F_t+\varepsilon_{0t}\), the loss contrast is
\[
 \ell_{1,t}-\ell_{2,t}
 =-2\eta_0U_t(e_{1t}-e_{2t})+eta_0^2(e_{1t}^2-e_{2t}^2).
\]
The summands are uncorrelated, \(\operatorname{Var}(e_1-e_2)=2x_0\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(e_1^2-e_2^2)=4x_0^2\).  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(D)
 =4\eta_0^2\{(1-\eta_0)^2B_0+\bar b_0\}(2x_0)
 +4\eta_0^4x_0^2.
\]
Since \((1-\eta_0)^2B_0+\bar b_0=159119/160000\),
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(D)=\frac{159119}{2560000}+\frac1{4096}
 =\frac{39}{625}>\nu.
\]
The post residual is \(v_{s,t}=\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{s,t}\), whose ordinary-row variance is \(\bar b_0+x_0=1\).  With \(r=1\) and \(A_s=0\),
\[
 V_s=V_s^{\mathrm{gap}}=1>\nu.
\]
All defining conditions of \(\mathcal M(0)\) now hold.  The factor representation, constant effect, conditional error independence, nonzero square bridge, and rowwise domination established in \(\texttt{prop:shi-anchor-transfer}\) also place these arrays in the stated common published subclass.

Analyze row \(q\).  Let \(\mathcal N_q\) be the event that \(I_{q,t}=0\) for every \(t\in\mathcal B_q\cup\mathcal C_q\).  It is independent of \(\mathcal F_A\), and, because the two future blocks contain at most \(2q\) observations,
\[
 \Pr(\mathcal N_q)\geq(1-q^{-2})^{2q}\to1.
\]
The early label is \(\mathcal F_A\)-measurable.  Fix either possible selected donor \(j\), with opposite proxy \(k\).  On \(\mathcal N_q\), the true bridge residual is
\[
 r_{j,t}^0=-p_q+a_q(Z_{0t}-Z_{jt}).
\]
The exact future-only bridge definition gives, except on the null event \(\widehat M_{B,j}=0\),
\[
 \widehat\alpha_{B,j}-\alpha_j
 =\widehat M_{B,j}^{-1}N_{B,q}^{-1}
  \sum_{t\in\mathcal B_q}W_{kt}r_{j,t}^0.
\]
Conditional on \(\mathcal N_q\), Gaussian laws and Chebyshev's inequality give
\[
 \widehat M_{B,j}=c_0^2B_0+O_P(q^{-1/2}),quad
 \overline W_{k,B}=O_P(q^{-1/2}),quad
 \widehat\alpha_{B,j}-\alpha_j
 =O_P\{(p_q+a_q)q^{-1/2}\},
\]
uniformly over \(j=1,2\).  Similarly \(\overline W_{j,C}=O_P(q^{-1/2})\).  Hence the exact post average satisfies
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widehat\tau_{B,C,j}-\tau
 &=\overline r_{j,C}^0-(\widehat\alpha_{B,j}-\alpha_j)\overline W_{j,C}\\
 &=-p_q+O_P(a_qq^{-1/2})+O_P\{(p_q+a_q)q^{-1}\}
 =-p_q\{1+o_P(1)\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]

For any centered scalar observations \(g_1,\ldots,g_N\), the Bartlett quadratic form obeys
\[
 0\leq\widehat\Omega_g\leq(2h+1)N^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^Ng_t^2,
\]
by \(2|g_tg_{t-j}|\leq g_t^2+g_{t-j}^2\).  The centered fitted post residual differs from \(a_q(Z_{0t}-Z_{jt})\) by the centered version of \(-(\widehat\alpha_{B,j}-\alpha_j)W_{jt}\).  Therefore
\[
 \widehat\Omega_{v,C,j}
 =O_P\left[h_q\left\{a_q^2+\frac{(p_q+a_q)^2}{q}\right\}\right].
\]
The precise future-only sensitivity is \(\widehat H_{B,C,j}=-\widehat\mu_{C,j}^{\prime}\widehat M_{B,j}^{-1}=O_P(q^{-1/2})\).  Before its multiplication, the fitted bridge score has conditional second moment \(O_P(p_q^2+a_q^2)\), so
\[
 \widehat\Omega_{\psi,B,j}=O_P\{h_q(p_q^2+a_q^2)/q\}.
\]
Since \(N_{B,q}\asymp q\), \(m_q=q\), \(h_q=O(q^{1/5})\), and \(a_q\leq p_q\),
\[
 \widehat S_{j,q}^2
 =O_P\left\{\frac{h_qa_q^2}{q}+\frac{h_qp_q^2}{q^2}\right\},
 \qquad
 \frac{\widehat S_{j,q}}{p_q}=o_P(1).
\]
Because \(a_q>0\), the centered post residual vector contains a nonconstant continuous Gaussian component almost surely.  The Bartlett quadratic form is nonnegative and its zero set is a proper algebraic subset of that continuous vector; hence \(\widehat S_{j,q}>0\) almost surely for large \(q\), so the nonpositive fallback is not invoked.  Combining numerator and denominator bounds yields, on \(\mathcal N_q\),
\[
 T_q=\frac{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}-\tau}
 {\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_{\widehat J_A}}\to-\infty
\]
in probability, uniformly over both possible early labels.  Since \(\Pr(\mathcal N_q)\to1\), the same divergence holds unconditionally.

Choose deterministic \(b_q\to\infty\) so slowly that \(\Pr(T_q>-b_q)\to0\), and put
\[
 K_q=\sup_x\left|\Pr(T_q\leq x\mid\mathcal F_A)-\Phi(x)\right|.
\]
Evaluation at \(-b_q\) and Jensen's inequality give
\[
 \mathbb EK_q\geq
 \left|\Pr(T_q\leq-b_q)-\Phi(-b_q)\right|\to1.
\]
Since every Kolmogorov distance is at most one, \(\mathbb EK_q\to1\).  This is the asserted maximal failure.

For a whole array \(P_\bullet\), define
\[
 \mathcal K_n(P_\bullet)=
 \mathbb E_{P_n}\left[
  \sup_x\left|
   \Pr_{P_n}\left\{
    \frac{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}-\tau}
         {\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_{\widehat J_A}}
    \leq x\,\middle|\,\mathcal F_A
   \right\}-\Phi(x)
  \right|
 \right].
\]
It lies in \([0,1]\).  By \(\texttt{thm:maximal-uniform-singular-mapping-failure}\), for every sufficiently large \(q\) there is \(P_\bullet^{(q)}\in\mathcal M(0)\) with \(\mathcal K_q(P_\bullet^{(q)})\to1\), together with all structural and numerical witness properties in the theorem.

The only member restriction in \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\) depending on \(D_{\mathrm{gap}}\) is
\[
 \sup_{j\geq1}\sqrt j\,|L_{1,j}-L_{2,j}|\leq D_{\mathrm{gap}}.
\]
Every array in \(\mathcal M(0)\) satisfies it for any \(D_{\mathrm{gap}}\geq0\), so \(\mathcal M(0)\subseteq\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\).  Thus, with
\[
 S_n(D_{\mathrm{gap}})=\sup_{P_\bullet\in\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})}\mathcal K_n(P_\bullet),
\]
we have
\[
 1\geq S_q(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\geq\mathcal K_q(P_\bullet^{(q)})\to1.
\]
Because \(q\) ranges over every sufficiently large integer, \(S_n(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\to1\).  The witness concerns this paper's gap-split procedure over its broad reduced-form class.  The common-subclass certificate does not assert failure of a published fixed-role estimator or guarantee.

Fix \(s\in\mathcal S\).  Before treatment, \(Y_t=Y_t(0)\).  Define
\[
 \widehat K_s=I_{d_s}+n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nW_{D_s,t}W_{D_s,t}^{\prime},
 \qquad
 \widehat b_s=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nW_{D_s,t}Y_t(0).
\]
The empirical ridge criterion has Hessian \(2\widehat K_s\succeq2I_{d_s}\), so its unique minimizer is \(\widehat a_s=\widehat K_s^{-1}\widehat b_s\).  If \(U_t,V_t\) are centered scalar functions of observations separated by \(j\) periods and have uniformly bounded \((2+\epsilon)\)-moments, truncation at a common level, the total-variation definition of absolute regularity, H\"older's inequality, and optimization over the truncation level give
\[
 |\operatorname{Cov}_{P_n}(U_t,V_{t-j})|
 \leq C\beta_n(j)^{\epsilon/(2+\epsilon)}.
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:geometric-beta-mixing}\) this is bounded by \(C_1e^{-c_1j}\), uniformly in \(n\).  Fixed dimension and \(\texttt{ass:moment-bound}\), applied to the quadratic entries of \(W_{D_s,t}W_{D_s,t}^{\prime}\) and \(W_{D_s,t}Y_t(0)\), imply
\[
 \widehat K_s-K_s=O_{P_n}(n^{-1/2}),
 \qquad \widehat b_s-b_s=O_{P_n}(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Indeed the variance of each centered sample mean is at most \(n^{-1}\{\gamma(0)+2\sum_{j\geq1}|\gamma(j)|\}\leq C/n\), so Chebyshev's inequality applies.  Since \(K_s\succeq I_{d_s}\), \(\|K_s^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq1\), and Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(\|b_s\|_2\leq C\).  Therefore \(\|a_s\|_2\leq C\), and the exact normal-equation identity
\[
 \widehat a_s-a_s
 =\widehat K_s^{-1}\{(\widehat b_s-b_s)
  -(\widehat K_s-K_s)a_s\}
\]
shows \(\widehat a_s-a_s=O_{P_n}(n^{-1/2})\).  Completing the empirical quadratic about its minimizer gives
\[
 \widehat L_s
 =\widehat Q_s(a_s)
  -(\widehat a_s-a_s)^{\prime}\widehat K_s(\widehat a_s-a_s).
\]
The last term is \(O_{P_n}(n^{-1})\), while the definition of \(\ell_{s,t}\) gives
\[
 \widehat Q_s(a_s)-L_s=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^n(\ell_{s,t}-L_s).
\]
Multiplication by \(\sqrt n\) proves the claimed expansion.  Since \(\mathcal S=\{1,2\}\), taking the maximum of the two remainder probabilities proves joint validity.

added_lemmas.proof_tex: The sets \(\mathcal B_n\) and \(\mathcal C_n\) are deterministic.  For fixed \(s\), \(\widehat M_{B,s}\), its invertibility indicator, the inverse on that event, the fixed zero fallback, and \(\widehat\alpha_{B,s}\) are Borel functions of \((X_t:t\in\mathcal B_n)\).  The vector \(\widehat\mu_{C,s}\) is a Borel function of \((X_t:t\in\mathcal C_n)\).  Hence \(\widehat H_{B,C,s}\), including its fixed fallback, is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(X_t:t\in\mathcal B_n\cup\mathcal C_n)\).  The displayed finite sums defining \(\widehat u_{B,s,t}\), \(\widehat\psi_{B,s,t}\), \(\widehat\tau_{B,C,s}\), \(\widehat v_{C,s,t}\), their sample means and lag products, the two Bartlett estimates, and the piecewise square-root fallback are compositions of Borel maps of the same future observations.  Thus \(T_{s,n}^{\mathrm{gap}}\) is future-measurable.  Finally \(\widehat J_A\) is defined from the observations generating \(\mathcal F_A\), and substitution into the fixed-role formula gives \(T_{\widehat J_A,n}^{\mathrm{gap}}\).

Write \(N_B=N_{B,n}\).  The common horizon inequalities and the definition of \(\mathcal B_n\) give, uniformly over the class,
\[
 N_B/n\to1-\varrho,
 \qquad c_m\leq m/n\leq C_m
\]
for all \(n\geq n_\star\).  The moment bound, Cauchy--Schwarz, and \(\|M_s^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\kappa^{-1}\) imply common bounds on \(\alpha_s,\mu_s,H_s\).  Consequently there is \(\epsilon>0\) such that both \(\psi_{s,t}\) and \(v_{s,t}\) have uniformly bounded \((2+\epsilon)\)-moments.  Because they are measurable functions of \(X_t\), their absolute-regularity coefficients are bounded by those of \(X_t\).

The covariance truncation argument used in \(\texttt{lem:ridge-loss-expansion}\) yields, uniformly over rows, roles, and lags,
\[
 |\operatorname{Cov}(g_t,g_{t-j})|\leq C e^{-cj}
\]
for any centered scalar coordinate \(g_t\) among the oracle scores and the finite collection of moment coordinates used below.  It follows by summing covariances and applying Chebyshev's inequality that
\[
 \widehat M_{B,s}-M_s=O_P(N_B^{-1/2}),quad
 \widehat\mu_{C,s}-\mu_s=O_P(m^{-1/2}),quad
 N_B^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal B_n}u_{s,t}=O_P(N_B^{-1/2}),
\]
uniformly for \(s=1,2\).  The rank margin implies that the probability of the inverse fallback tends uniformly to zero.  On the invertibility event the bridge equation gives exactly
\[
 \widehat\alpha_{B,s}-\alpha_s
 =\widehat M_{B,s}^{-1}N_B^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal B_n}u_{s,t},
\]
so \(\widehat\alpha_{B,s}-\alpha_s=O_P(N_B^{-1/2})\), and matrix inversion gives
\[
 \widehat H_{B,C,s}-H_s=O_P(N_B^{-1/2}+m^{-1/2}).
\]
Using bridge centering and \(\tau=\mathbb E_n\Delta_t\), the post identity is
\[
 \widehat\tau_{B,C,s}-\tau
 =m^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal C_n}v_{s,t}
 -\widehat\mu_{C,s}^{\prime}(\widehat\alpha_{B,s}-\alpha_s).
\]
Substituting the exact bridge equation and \(H_s=-\mu_s^{\prime}M_s^{-1}\) shows
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{B,C,s}-\tau)=G_{s,n}+r_{s,n},
 \qquad
 \max_{s\in\mathcal S}|r_{s,n}|=o_P(1)
\]
uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{stab}}(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\).  Every product in the remainder contains one \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) moment-estimation error and one \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) score mean before multiplication by \(\sqrt n\).

We next prove a uniform scalar Gaussian approximation for \(G_{s,n}\).  Its summands have deterministic weights bounded by \(C n^{-1/2}\).  Partition \(\mathcal B_n\cup\mathcal C_n\) into consecutive large blocks of length \(\ell_n=\lfloor n^{1/3}\rfloor\), separated by gaps of length \(g_n=\lceil(\log n)^2\rceil\), allowing one block boundary at the change from the pre-score to the post-score.  Exponential covariance decay makes the variance of the omitted normalized gaps \(O(g_n/\ell_n)=o(1)\).  For bounded complex functions of successive retained blocks, the total-variation definition of \(\beta\) gives recursively
\[
 \left|\mathbb E\prod_{j=1}^{K_n}f_j-prod_{j=1}^{K_n}\mathbb Ef_j\right|
 \leq2(K_n-1)\beta_n(g_n)
 \leq Cn e^{-c(\log n)^2}=o(1).
\]
Applied to characteristic functions, this compares the retained sum with a sum of independent variables having the retained block marginals.

For completeness, truncation at \(\ell_n^{1/(2+\epsilon)}\), expansion of products, and the same covariance inequality give the block moment bound
\[
 \mathbb E|B_{j,n}|^{2+\epsilon}\leq
 C(\ell_n/n)^{1+\epsilon/2}
\]
for each normalized retained block sum \(B_{j,n}\).  Hence
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^{K_n}\mathbb E|B_{j,n}|^{2+\epsilon}
 \leq C(\ell_n/n)^{\epsilon/2}\to0.
\]
Taylor's formula for the characteristic function of each independent centered block, followed by multiplication, proves a normal limit after division by the independent-block standard deviation.  The variance removed with the gaps is \(o(1)\), and the sum of all cross-block covariances discarded by independence is bounded by
\[
 C K_n\sum_{h\geq g_n}e^{-ch}=o(1).
\]
Therefore the independent-block variance differs from \(W_{s,n}\) by \(o(1)\), uniformly.  Since \(\underline w\leq W_{s,n}\leq\overline w\), division is uniformly safe.  The characteristic-function conclusion plus continuity of \(\Phi\), applied along an arbitrary allegedly failing sequence of rows and laws, yields the uniform Kolmogorov conclusion
\[
 \max_{s\in\mathcal S}\sup_{P_\bullet\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{stab}}}
 \sup_x\left|\Pr_{P_n}\{G_{s,n}/\sqrt{W_{s,n}}\leq x\}-\Phi(x)\right|\to0.
\]
This subsequence argument requires no convergence, and no inverse, of the covariance obtained by stacking the roles.

It remains to justify fitted Bartlett studentization.  Let \(\widetilde\Omega_{\psi,B,s}\) and \(\widetilde\Omega_{v,C,s}\) denote the same Bartlett formulas computed from centered oracle \(\psi_{s,t}\) and \(v_{s,t}\).  Exponential covariance decay gives the uniform bias bound
\[
 \left|\mathbb E\widetilde\Omega_{g}-\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Cov}(g_t,g_{t-j})\right|
 \leq C\{h_n^{-1}+h_n/N+e^{-ch_n}\},
\]
where \(N=N_B\) or \(m\).  Expanding the covariance of the lag-product averages and applying the same truncation inequality to fourfold products gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\widetilde\Omega_g)\leq C h_n^2/N=o(1),
\]
because \(h_n\asymp n^{1/5}\).  Thus each oracle Bartlett estimate is uniformly consistent for its row long-run variance.

The exact finite-block variance satisfies
\[
 W_{s,n}=n\operatorname{Var}\left(N_B^{-1}\sum_{\mathcal B_n}\psi_{s,t}\right)
 +n\operatorname{Var}\left(m^{-1}\sum_{\mathcal C_n}v_{s,t}\right)+o(1).
\]
Indeed the omitted cross covariance is bounded by
\[
 \frac{Cn}{N_Bm}\sum_{a\geq0}\sum_{b\geq1}e^{-c(a+b)}=O(n^{-1}),
\]
and the difference between either finite-block variance and its Bartlett-weighted long-run expression is \(o(1)\) by the preceding bias calculation.  Consequently
\[
 n\left\{\frac{\widetilde\Omega_{\psi,B,s}}{N_B}
 +\frac{\widetilde\Omega_{v,C,s}}m\right\}-W_{s,n}=o_P(1)
\]
uniformly.

The already proved parameter rates and Cauchy--Schwarz imply
\[
 N_B^{-1}\sum_{\mathcal B_n}(\widehat\psi_{B,s,t}-\psi_{s,t})^2=o_P(1),
 \qquad
 m^{-1}\sum_{\mathcal C_n}(\widehat v_{C,s,t}-v_{s,t})^2=o_P(1)
\]
uniformly.  For two centered sequences \(a_t,b_t\), summing \(|a_tb_{t-j}|\leq(a_t^2+b_{t-j}^2)/2\) over the \(h_n\) lags bounds the Bartlett replacement error by \(C h_n\) times the root mean-square score error times a uniformly tight score norm.  The parameter errors above are \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\), so \(h_n=O(n^{1/5})\) makes both fitted-score replacement errors \(o_P(1)\).  Therefore
\[
 \max_s|n\widehat S_{s,n}^2-W_{s,n}|=o_P(1).
\]
The lower bound \(W_{s,n}\geq\underline w\) makes the nonpositive fallback probability tend uniformly to zero.

Let \(U_{s,n}=G_{s,n}/\sqrt{W_{s,n}}\).  The linearization and variance conclusion imply that the fitted statistic differs from \(U_{s,n}\) by \(o_P(1)\), uniformly.  For every \(\delta>0\), normal anti-concentration gives
\[
 \sup_x|\Pr(T_{s,n}^{\mathrm{gap}}\leq x)-\Phi(x)|
 \leq \sup_x|\Pr(U_{s,n}\leq x)-\Phi(x)|
 +\Pr(|T_{s,n}^{\mathrm{gap}}-U_{s,n}|>\delta)
 +\frac{\delta}{\sqrt{2\pi}}.
\]
First sending \(n\to\infty\), then \(\delta\downarrow0\), proves uniform unconditional studentized normality.

By \(\texttt{lem:gap-future-measurability}\), the fixed-role statistic is measurable with respect to the future sigma-field beginning after the discarded gap.  Absolute regularity therefore gives, uniformly in \(x\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_n}\left|
 \Pr_{P_n}(T_{s,n}^{\mathrm{gap}}\leq x\mid\mathcal F_A)
 -\Pr_{P_n}(T_{s,n}^{\mathrm{gap}}\leq x)
 \right|\leq2\beta_n(b_n)=o(1).
\]
Monotonicity of distribution functions lets the same bound transfer to the supremum over \(x\) by evaluating first on a finite normal-quantile grid and controlling the intervening normal increments.  Thus the expected conditional Kolmogorov distance tends uniformly to zero for each role.  Since \(\widehat J_A\) is \(\mathcal F_A\)-measurable,
\[
 \Pr(T_{\widehat J_A,n}^{\mathrm{gap}}\leq x\mid\mathcal F_A)
 =\sum_{s=1}^2\mathbf1\{\widehat J_A=s\}
  \Pr(T_{s,n}^{\mathrm{gap}}\leq x\mid\mathcal F_A),
\]
so its distance is bounded by the maximum of the two fixed-role distances.  This proves the asserted selected result.

For nonemptiness, take the symmetric primitive Gaussian law \(\theta_0\), \(m_n=n\), and the precise future-only definitions above.  The sample inverse fallback and variance fallback have probabilities tending to zero by the scalar positive bridge moment and positive Gaussian score variance.  Independence makes all cross-block covariances zero, and direct substitution from \(\texttt{prop:primitive-realizations}\) gives
\[
 W_{s,n}\to\frac{3}{2(1-\varrho)}+2>0,
 \qquad s=1,2.
\]
Choose \(n_\star\) and common \(\underline w,\overline w\) around this limit and take \(c_m\leq1\leq C_m\).  All other class conditions hold by the primitive and anchor propositions.  Hence the strengthened class is nonempty.

proposed.name: bounded-gap triangular-array proximal role-selection class
proposed.construction:
For each fixed \(D_{\mathrm{gap}}<\infty\),
\[
 \mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})
 =\{(P_n)_{n\geq1}:(P_n)_{n\geq1}\text{ satisfies }
 \texttt{ass:stationarity},\texttt{ass:geometric-beta-mixing},
 \texttt{ass:moment-bound},\texttt{ass:sample-ratio},
 \texttt{ass:bridge-rank},\texttt{ass:bridge-centering},
 \texttt{ass:bounded-selector-gap-array},
 \texttt{ass:covariance-limit},\texttt{ass:att-variance-margin},
 \text{ and }\texttt{ass:selector-variance-margin}\}.
\]
The ratio and covariance conditions in this broad class are arraywise limiting conditions.  In particular, \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\) does not impose horizon-comparability constants and a threshold common to every array in a rowwise supremum, nor does it impose common finite-row lower and upper bounds on the scalar late/post influence variance.  Those additional restrictions define \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{stab}}(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\) in \(\texttt{def:panel-stabilized-class}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The broad class must explicitly distinguish pointwise horizon limits from the common rowwise stabilization needed by the positive theorem.

proposed.name: early-select, late-fit proximal ATT
proposed.construction:
Put \(a_n=\lfloor\varrho n\rfloor\), \(b_n=\lceil(\log n)^2\rceil\), \(\mathcal B_n=\{a_n+b_n+1,\ldots,n\}\), \(N_{B,n}=|\mathcal B_n|\), and \(\mathcal C_n=\{n+1,\ldots,n+m\}\).  For each fixed role \(s\in\mathcal S\), define
\[
 \widehat M_{B,s}=N_{B,n}^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal B_n}Z_{s,t}W_{D_s,t}^{\prime}.
\]
If \(\widehat M_{B,s}\) is invertible, let
\[
 \widehat\alpha_{B,s}
 =\widehat M_{B,s}^{-1}N_{B,n}^{-1}
   \sum_{t\in\mathcal B_n}Z_{s,t}Y_t;
\]
otherwise set \(\widehat\alpha_{B,s}=0\).  Define
\[
 \widehat\mu_{C,s}=m^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal C_n}W_{D_s,t},
 \qquad
 \widehat H_{B,C,s}=-\widehat\mu_{C,s}^{\prime}\widehat M_{B,s}^{-1}
\]
when \(\widehat M_{B,s}\) is invertible, and set \(\widehat H_{B,C,s}=0\) otherwise.  For \(t\in\mathcal B_n\), put
\[
 \widehat u_{B,s,t}=Z_{s,t}
  (Y_t-W_{D_s,t}^{\prime}\widehat\alpha_{B,s}),
 \qquad
 \widehat\psi_{B,s,t}=\widehat H_{B,C,s}\widehat u_{B,s,t}.
\]
The counterfactual fixed-role estimate and the selected estimate are
\[
 \widehat\tau_{B,C,s}=m^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal C_n}
 (Y_t-W_{D_s,t}^{\prime}\widehat\alpha_{B,s}),
 \qquad
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}=\widehat\tau_{B,C,\widehat J_A}.
\]
For \(t\in\mathcal C_n\), put
\[
 \widehat v_{C,s,t}=Y_t-W_{D_s,t}^{\prime}\widehat\alpha_{B,s}
 -\widehat\tau_{B,C,s}.
\]
Let \(\overline{\widehat\psi}_{B,s}=N_{B,n}^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal B_n}\widehat\psi_{B,s,t}\).  For \(0\leq j\leq h_n\), define
\[
 \widehat\gamma_{\psi,B,s}(j)=N_{B,n}^{-1}
 \sum_{\substack{t,t-j\in\mathcal B_n}}
 (\widehat\psi_{B,s,t}-\overline{\widehat\psi}_{B,s})
 (\widehat\psi_{B,s,t-j}-\overline{\widehat\psi}_{B,s}),
\]
\[
 \widehat\gamma_{v,C,s}(j)=m^{-1}
 \sum_{t=n+j+1}^{n+m}\widehat v_{C,s,t}\widehat v_{C,s,t-j}.
\]
The Bartlett estimates are
\[
 \widehat\Omega_{\psi,B,s}=\widehat\gamma_{\psi,B,s}(0)
 +2\sum_{j=1}^{h_n}\left(1-\frac{j}{h_n+1}\right)
 \widehat\gamma_{\psi,B,s}(j),
\]
\[
 \widehat\Omega_{v,C,s}=\widehat\gamma_{v,C,s}(0)
 +2\sum_{j=1}^{h_n}\left(1-\frac{j}{h_n+1}\right)
 \widehat\gamma_{v,C,s}(j).
\]
Set
\[
 \widehat S_{s,n}^2
 =\frac{\widehat\Omega_{\psi,B,s}}{N_{B,n}}
  +\frac{\widehat\Omega_{v,C,s}}m,
 \qquad
 \widehat{\operatorname{se}}_s=
 \begin{cases}
  \sqrt{\widehat S_{s,n}^2},&\widehat S_{s,n}^2>0,\\
  1,&\widehat S_{s,n}^2\leq0
 \end{cases}
\]
(with the second branch also used for any nonfinite arithmetic value), and report
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}-\tau}
 {\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_{\widehat J_A}}.
\]
Thus no full-pre-period fitted sensitivity or score enters the gap-split statistic, and every inverse and nonpositive-variance case has a fixed measurable fallback.

proposed.name: finite-row stabilized bounded-gap panel class
proposed.construction:
Fix constants \(0<c_m\leq C_m<\infty\), \(0<\underline w\leq\overline w<\infty\), and an integer \(n_\star\), all common to the class.  For row \(n\) and role \(s\), define the oracle future linear statistic and its finite-row variance by
\[
 G_{s,n}=\sqrt n\left\{
  N_{B,n}^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal B_n}\psi_{s,t}
  +m^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal C_n}v_{s,t}
 \right\},
 \qquad
 W_{s,n}=\operatorname{Var}_{P_n}(G_{s,n}).
\]
Then \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{stab}}(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\) is the subclass of \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\) consisting of arrays for which, for every \(n\geq n_\star\) and both \(s\in\mathcal S\),
\[
 c_m\leq \frac mn\leq C_m,
 \qquad
 \underline w\leq W_{s,n}\leq\overline w.
\]
The constants and threshold are fixed before the supremum over arrays is taken.  These are primitive horizon and scalar variance restrictions; no Gaussian approximation, covariance nonsingularity for the stacked roles, or HAC consistency is included in the definition.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The positive theorem requires common finite-row horizon and scalar variance bounds, without assuming its Gaussian or HAC conclusions.

prose_updates.tldr: Two predeclared valid proximal synthetic-control role assignments can identify the same ATT yet yield a nonregular conventional interval when the smaller full-pre-period ridge loss selects the reported role. The exact selected-Gaussian coverage map protects every symmetric Wald level at an exact tie and protects every local gap exactly when the two standardized ATT coordinates have equal squared selector correlations; otherwise the strict coverage-error sign is the gap sign times their squared-correlation difference. A constant-treatment one-factor Gaussian chart realizes both regimes inside a stationary square subclass of the Shi et al. model, including an open asymmetric region with coverage \(0.8857757910650707\) for a nominal \(90\%\) interval. For correction, an early selector, logarithm-squared gap, late bridge fit, post average, and future-only Bartlett standard error are uniformly selector-conditionally normal on the strengthened class with common finite-row horizon and scalar variance bounds. The same claim fails maximally on the broader pointwise-limit class, where expected conditional Kolmogorov distance can converge to one.

project_justification.gap: Published proximal synthetic-control theory predetermines donor and supplemental-proxy roles, while general post-selection results do not characterize exact ordinary symmetric-Wald coverage when a loss comparison switches between two valid proximal ATT coordinates. Pointwise horizon and limiting-variance conditions also do not support a supremum over whole triangular arrays.
project_justification.niche: The binary ridge selector admits an exact squared-correlation coverage frontier. A future-only split construction admits uniform coordinatewise studentization after imposing common finite-row horizon comparability and scalar influence-variance bounds, while singular covariance across the stacked roles remains allowed.
project_justification.fill: The paper gives the selected limit, evaluable coverage functional, all-gap if-and-only-if frontier, strict error sign, primitive open miscoverage family, and a positive/negative uniformity boundary. The corrected estimator is uniformly selector-conditionally normal on \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{stab}}(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\); a diagonal common-subclass witness proves maximal failure on \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\).

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The conventional procedure uses all pre-period observations both to select and fit. The corrected procedure selects on the first \(\lfloor\varrho n\rfloor\) observations, discards \(\lceil(\log n)^2\rceil\), estimates \(\widehat M_{B,s}\) and \(\widehat\alpha_{B,s}\) on the late block, estimates \(\widehat\mu_{C,s}\) on the post block, forms \(\widehat H_{B,C,s}\), and computes separate future-only fitted pre and post scores. Bartlett estimates with \(h_n=\lfloor\min(N_{B,n},m)^{1/5}\rfloor\) are scaled by \(N_{B,n}^{-1}\) and \(m^{-1}\); every inverse and nonpositive-variance case has a fixed measurable fallback.

prose_updates.related_work: Shi et al. (2026) supply the fixed-role structural proximal anchor; the common-subclass proposition, not a full-class inclusion claim, transfers the present phenomena to legal stationary square panels. Leeb and Pötscher (2005) motivate local post-selection nonregularity, whereas Rakshit, Shi, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2025) address the distinct problem of adaptive selection with potentially invalid proxies. Berk et al. (2013) obtain post-selection protection by simultaneous inference, not by characterizing when an ordinary selected Wald interval is already exact. Lee et al. (2016), Leeb, Pötscher, and Ewald (2015), and Azzalini and Regoli (2012) provide related Gaussian conditioning, coverage, and symmetry tools but not the switched proximal squared-correlation frontier. Lunde (2019) and Andrews (1991) motivate separated-block dependence control and Bartlett estimation. Here those ingredients are derived for the precise future-only proximal statistic on a stabilized class, while the diagonal theorem shows why pointwise array limits alone are insufficient.
prose_updates.interpretation: For a predeclared pair of scientifically credible donor/proxy roles, conventional two-sided Wald inference is robust to local selection exactly on the squared-correlation frontier, even though the selected statistic can have nonzero mean. Off that frontier the sign formula diagnoses under- or overcoverage. If that covariance diagnostic is not defensible, the gap-split interval has a uniform justification only after the design fixes common horizon comparability and verifies finite-row scalar influence-variance margins.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The positive theorem is uniform only over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{stab}}(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\), whose horizon constants, threshold, and finite-row scalar variance bounds are common before the supremum is taken. It does not require nonsingularity of the stacked role covariance, but it does require fixed dimension, uniform geometric beta mixing, the declared high moment and bridge-rank margins, and future-only fitted scores. The broad class \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\) retains only arraywise limiting horizon and covariance conditions; the diagonal counterexample exploits that difference and makes the conditional approximation error maximal.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact coverage result concerns two predeclared square bridges, ridge penalty one, bounded root-\(n\) selector gaps, and positive marginal selector and ATT variances. The conventional interval reuses the full pre period. The corrected interval uses a fixed early fraction, a logarithm-squared gap, late bridge fitting, post residual averaging, and bandwidth exponent one fifth; its uniform theorem additionally fixes common finite-row horizon and scalar oracle-variance bounds. The Gaussian chart and diagonal witness lie in an explicit stationary constant-effect intersection with Shi et al.'s fixed-role class, but no wholesale class extension or refutation of a published fixed-role guarantee is claimed. The analysis does not cover the rectangular simplex-constrained West-German rule, estimate the local drift, restore full-pre-period efficiency, or handle more than two roles. Its actionable use is a predeclared two-candidate robustness analysis before retaining the negative GDP conclusion.

statement_notes.gap: Leeb and Pötscher provide the generic local post-selection perspective, Rakshit et al. study selection with potentially invalid proxies, and Berk et al. use simultaneous protection. None gives this switched valid-role proximal ATT law; the Shi comparison is restricted to the proved common subclass.

statement_notes.consumer: Together with the stabilized-class theorem, this establishes a positive/negative design boundary based on common finite-row horizon comparability and scalar variance stabilization for the proposed correction.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem supplies a complete positive counterpart to the broad-class converse using a precisely future-measurable estimator and coordinatewise normalization that remains valid under singular stacked covariance.
statement_notes.gap: Generic splitting and HAC results do not by themselves compose the proximal inverse, fitted-score replacement, random early label, and whole-array supremum; the proof closes those steps under explicit primitive stabilization.
statement_notes.consumer: An analyst can predeclare two roles, select early, fit and studentize only on future blocks, and report a uniformly justified interval after verifying the common horizon and finite-row scalar variance margins.
